Definition: middle voice of a primary verb (used only in the present and imperfect tenses, the others being supplied by a kindred (middle voice) ἐλεύθομαι, or (active) ἔλθω, which do not otherwise occur); to come or go (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively):--accompany, appear, bring, come, enter, fall out, go, grow, X light, X next, pass, resort, be set.
BiblicalUsage: Érchomai is the word for coming — the common verb for arriving, appearing, and approaching. John the Baptist came; Jesus came; the kingdom comes; and the last word of the Bible is a promise that He will come quickly. It is the verb of the whole story, from the first coming to the second.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe érchomai is the heartbeat of the gospel: God comes to us, and we are to watch for His coming again. I hold that every 'come' in Scripture is either a promise kept or a promise still to be kept.
